basis: Ischemic necrosis and fibrosis of forearm skeletal muscles cause permanent contracture; vascular occlusion is a cause, not an additional defining organ disease.
Congenital myopathy with contractures; cardiomyopathy in 8/8. Respiratory distress and motor/speech delays do not establish intrinsic lung or central nervous system damage.
Tentative identification as a skeletal and developmental malformation syndrome; supplied record lacks a definition, phenotypes or informative ancestors.
Carcinoma arises in the floor of the mouth; oral tissues and salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Joubert syndrome defines a hindbrain developmental disorder. Eye movement abnormalities and breathing dysregulation are neurologic; coloboma and hearing loss are uncommon.
Malignant tumor originates in lung or pleura. Other DICER1-associated tumors are separate diseases, and additional lesions occur in only about 25%.
Immunodeficiency with defining ectodermal dysplasia; developmental impairment is supported by speech delay in 5/5 and motor delay in 4/4. Recurrent infections are separately diagnosed.
Inherited fucosylation disorders are metabolic diseases; developmental impairment is a common major phenotype across the group, exceeding the approximately 30% threshold.
Pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction causes excessive insulin secretion and hypoglycemia. Neurologic injury is a possible complication, not established as common here.
Arterial dysplasia defines disease; joint subluxation occurs in 3/6 and atrophic scarring in 2/6. Migraine does not establish brain injury.
Endocrine pancreatic tumor; necrolytic skin lesions, anemia and stomatitis/glossitis each occur in 30-79%. Thromboembolism is <30%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Developmental and cognitive impairment define the deletion syndrome; strabismus affects 80-99%. Facial features and palmar creases do not establish additional organ damage.
Progressive cerebellar and peripheral nerve disease; fixed pes cavus occurs in 30-79%. Saccadic abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Hyperplasia is located in the adrenal medulla, an endocrine gland.
Renal agenesis/dysplasia defines disease; oligohydramnios sequence includes pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/3 and structural clubfoot in 3/3.
Localized fibroepithelial lesion arises from gingiva, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Autoimmune destruction of platelets defines the condition. Bleeding manifestations do not independently establish chronic damage to other organs.
Accessory deep peroneal nerve is a peripheral nerve anatomical variant; no additional organ damage is established.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define disease. Cerebral visual impairment originates in the brain; facial traits and macrodontia do not establish other organ dysfunction.
ARMS2-associated degeneration of the retinal macula.
Nonsyndromic congenital absence or hypoplasia of central hand bones and digits; definition explicitly excludes other developmental abnormalities.
Cutaneous mucin deposition defines the umbrella disorder. Systemic involvement of scleromyxedema cannot be generalized to localized and atypical forms.
ALPL deficiency causes defective skeletal mineralization; dental attachment/mineralization defects and premature tooth loss are common, especially in surviving children.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and young-onset diabetes define the syndrome. Hearing loss and dental abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Deafness, synostoses and neurodevelopmental defects define syndrome; urethral hypospadias occurs in 80-99%. Cap excludes alopecia and dental abnormalities, each 30-79%.
